interest: Shows 1947 occupied-Japan welfare crises: defenses of the black market, war orphans, and neglected disabled veterans amid shortages.
overview: This file consists of an October 1947 transmittal despatch from the United States Political Adviser for Japan in Tokyo to the Department of State, an internal State Department routing note, and an enclosed GHQ/SCAP Civil Information and Education (CI&E) Section Publications Analysis (No. 91, dated January 24, 1947) entitled 'Welfare.' The report analyzes contemporary Japanese magazine articles regarding acute postwar domestic social problems. Major subjects include the crisis of war orphans and abandoned infants, rising juvenile delinquency, the inadequate institutional care and public indifference facing demobilized and disabled soldiers (highlighted by conditions at Sagamigahara National Hospital), the provisions of the new Law of Protection of Livelihood, and widespread journalistic defenses of open-air black markets as essential survival mechanisms for impoverished citizens.
